articleTitle: Chaos, competitiveness and control. The qualities of top management and how to blend them into a team
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers. Part 3 - The Transition into Corporate Management
abstract: From his experience as engineer, manager and management consultant the author believes that a director's job is to determine strategy, set up the environment for it's execution and then delegate the work to managers. This requires a blend of entrepreneur and leader with business, financial and chairmanship skills as well as professional specialist skills. To find these in one person is rare. A most important skill of the chief executive is to grow a team which provides these skills and then manage it so that conflict is productive rather than destructive. The author discusses the transition from manager to director, the qualities of the individual director, and blending the top management team.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Managers-a view from the City. A personal view of the attributes in managers of successful companies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers. Part 3 - The Transition into Corporate Management
abstract: The main attributes expected of managers by the City are the same as those required by industry itself-the ability to devise and execute effective management strategies and to communicate the results to others. The author explores the issue in detail, and considers what makes a successful company. The author suggests that the skills necessary to become and remain a successful manager, particularly in the private sector, are the ability to develop an appropriate plan, to communicate to others what the plan is, to do it effectively, and then to ensure that the success is recognised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An introduction to practical law for businesses
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers. Part 3 - The Transition into Corporate Management
abstract: The author gives an overview of the law governing businesses in the UK and in particular looks at the concept of the English company and the legal role of directors and managers within it. The author discusses: UK business media; the nature of the UK (English) company; and the powers and duties of company directors and managers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
